reasons: Wrong quantity: Datadog redis.net.clients counts connected clients, but the candidate uses redis.clients.blocked, which measures blocked clients.

The candidate PromQL ignores the $host filter (tag prefix host, default *), so the series set is not restricted to the host matcher the Datadog request applies. Matcher form should be host-based label =~"$host" if the dataset has that label; only redis_version is observed, so verify the label name before emitting it.

The outcome is translated although a direct OTel equivalent for connected clients appears to exist (redis.clients.connected, a non-monotonic sum in {client}); the candidate should translate to that metric, not to blocked clients.
The $key template variable (prefix key) is not applied in the query, so the matcher is missing there as well.
Aggregation sum over all series with no grouping matches the Datadog request, and the {client} unit is consistent with the Datadog metric.
